facts.name: data.rules[truck_ban.cars_free].text
facts.value: The ban does not apply to cars, motorhomes and vans under 7.5 t — for them Sunday is an ordinary driving day.

facts.name: data.rules[truck_ban.enforcement].text
facts.value: Breaches are penalised separately for driver and operator; enforcement happens at rest areas and border crossings.

facts.name: data.rules[truck_ban.enforcement].unconfirmed
facts.value: the amounts for driver and operator

facts.name: data.rules[truck_ban.exemptions].text
facts.value: Exempt are, among others, combined transport, fresh milk, fresh meat, fresh fruit and vegetables — and the empty runs that belong to them.

facts.name: data.rules[truck_ban.holidays].text
facts.value: The holidays nationwide are New Year, Good Friday, Easter Monday, 1 May, Ascension, Whit Monday, 3 October, 25 and 26 December; in some federal states only: Corpus Christi (Baden-Württemberg, Bavaria, Hesse, North Rhine-Westphalia, Rhineland-Palatinate, Saarland), Reformation Day on 31 October (Brandenburg, Bremen, Hamburg, Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, Lower Saxony, Saxony, Saxony-Anhalt, Schleswig-Holstein, Thuringia) and All Saints' Day on 1 November (Baden-Württemberg, Bavaria, North Rhine-Westphalia, Rhineland-Palatinate, Saarland).

facts.name: data.rules[truck_ban.state_holidays].text
facts.value: A holiday of some federal states only is a ban day only there: on 31 October the lorry ban from 00:00 to 22:00 applies in the nine states named; in Baden-Württemberg, Bavaria, Berlin, Hesse, North Rhine-Westphalia, Rhineland-Palatinate and Saarland the day is not a holiday under § 30(4) — unless it falls on a Sunday.

facts.name: data.rules[truck_ban.summer].text
facts.value: On top of that comes the holiday-season ban: 1 July to 31 August, Saturdays 07:00–20:00, on the motorway and federal-road sections listed in the regulation.

facts.name: data.rules[truck_ban.sunday].text
facts.value: On Sundays and public holidays, lorries over 7.5 t and lorries with trailers may not drive between 00:00 and 22:00.

facts.name: data.rules[truck_ban.unlisted_holidays].text
facts.value: A state holiday that § 30(4) does not name is not a lorry-ban day — in Bavaria, for example, Epiphany (6 January), Assumption Day (15 August, in municipalities with a predominantly Catholic population) and in Augsburg the Peace Festival (8 August).

facts.name: data.rules[lez.diesel_bans].text
facts.value: Some cities additionally had diesel through-traffic bans that apply regardless of the plaque and have changed repeatedly — check the city's own page before you drive.

facts.name: data.rules[lez.diesel_bans].unconfirmed
facts.value: which diesel bans are still in force today (Stuttgart, Munich, Hamburg among others)

facts.name: data.rules[lez.foreign_stickers].text
facts.value: A French Crit'Air sticker or any other foreign environmental badge is not valid in Germany — only the German Feinstaubplakette counts.

facts.name: data.rules[lez.green_only].text
facts.value: In practice every signposted Umweltzone today requires the green plaque (emission group 4). The supplementary sign under the zone sign is what actually decides which plaque applies.

facts.name: data.rules[lez.green_only].unconfirmed
facts.value: whether any single zone still admits yellow or red plaques — if in doubt, the supplementary sign decides

facts.name: data.rules[lez.penalty].text
facts.value: Entering the zone without a valid plaque costs a fine in the order of €100.

facts.name: data.rules[lez.penalty].unconfirmed
facts.value: the exact amount in the current fines catalogue

facts.name: data.rules[lez.price].text
facts.value: At an issuing office the fee is usually a few euros; online resellers charge considerably more.

facts.name: data.rules[lez.price].unconfirmed
facts.value: the exact fee charged per issuing office

facts.name: data.rules[lez.signage].text
facts.value: The zone starts at sign 270.1 and ends at sign 270.2; the plate underneath shows which plaques are admitted.

facts.name: data.rules[lez.where_to_buy].text
facts.value: You get the plaque at vehicle registration offices, technical inspection bodies (TÜV, DEKRA, GTÜ, KÜS) and approved garages. Bring the vehicle registration document (part I) or its foreign equivalent. It does not expire and belongs to that one vehicle.

facts.name: data.rules[lez.zones_exist].text
facts.value: Many German cities have a low-emission zone (Umweltzone): you may only drive in with a valid Feinstaubplakette displayed on the windscreen — foreign vehicles included.

cases.ruling: Lead ruling 2026-11-17: compared are the live-source families viafrei://coverage lists (family, staleAfterS, shareAlike); the reference families (bast_lcl, bkg_gvisys, delfi_static, geonames, osm, osm_speed_cameras, viafrei_rules), the domain and the domain filter are API-only. Lead ruling 2026-11-17 (round 3): its condition and purpose notes are register texts and are left out (meta.notes); a family not reviewed yet (no use class) is listed to ViaFrei's own keys, as the coverage resource lists it, and served to none.

cases.apiOnly: The domain filter is API-only (lead ruling 2026-11-17): viafrei://coverage states no domain, and the places domain holds only reference families, which the coverage resource does not list.

The MCP side has no matching form (the coverage resource counts places per platform kind, with no family or Land; the home's national tiles are HTML); site parity comes with the web switch to the API (lead ruling 2026-11-17).
